correctness.rationale: For every \(m\ge2\) and \(\alpha>-1\), the convex hull of the sampled parabola has precise lower and upper chords at the target abscissa. The resulting exact opposite-sign order-statistic density integrals give the finite-m law; two-corner boundary Laplace and interior quadratic Laplace expansions prove both leading constants and the unique \(\alpha=\sqrt2\) crossing. All hypotheses, endpoints and normalization are explicit; the stdlib checker passed 2,222 rational/numerical cases and the infinite-parameter proof does not rest on computations.

value.rationale: Random prescribed-node exact positive quadrature is a natural stability-sensitive numerical integration problem. The result gives exact success at every m and two analytically distinct failure mechanisms with a new, parameter-dependent exponential-scale phase boundary at \(\alpha=\sqrt2\). The sample-budget constants are unavailable from abstract high-probability existence frameworks; the positive result is a complete classification of an interpretable polynomial-degree-two family. No general algorithmic performance claim is made.
